title: Workload Rehearsal and Deterministic Replay Framework
author: Sofia Alvarez
content:
Summary:

This page documents the Workload Rehearsal and Deterministic Replay Framework (WRDR). WRDR provides a safe, repeatable way to replay historical production traffic—or synthesized equivalents—against staging or canary environments to validate changes to batching, kernel selection, routing policies, and cache/quantization profiles. The framework emphasizes deterministic input replay, observability parity, safety fences, and measurable pass/fail criteria tied to token cost, tail latency, and quality regressions.

Why this exists:
- Changes to the serving runtime (batching, KV cache sharding, kernel switching) can have non-linear effects on tail latency and cost.
- Unit tests and microbenchmarks miss emergent behavior from real multi-tenant traffic and inter-service dependencies.
- WRDR lets platform and runtime engineers validate regressions before large-scale rollouts and provides a forensics tool for incident reconstruction.

When to use WRDR:
- Before merging runtime patches that touch the batching layer, scheduler, or kernel selection heuristics.
- Prior to toggling global rollout flags (e.g., JIT kernel switching).
- For incident reenactments where traffic pattern needs reconstruction.
- As part of quarterly operator-run rehearsals and postmortem verification.

High-level design:
1) Input capture: ORION collector ingests representative traces with deterministic request payloads and anonymized context (no PII). Capture includes: request id, model id, sequence length, client hints, token counts, KV-prefix keys, and timestamp series.
2) Normalization: A replay manifest normalizes variable fields (timestamps, ephemeral IDs) and optionally synthesizes client-hint variations for edge-case coverage.
3) Deterministic driver: The WRDR driver replays requests with preserved inter-arrival timing (or accelerated modes) and enforces ordering where required (e.g., prefix cache priming sequences).
4) Isolation harness: Replays run in a constrained canary/staging tenancy with traffic throttles, quota knobs, and network egress controls.
5) Observability parity: During replays we materialize the same metrics, distributed traces, and cost-attribution signals into the platform observability stack.
6) Analysis engine: Post-run diffs compute delta on SLIs/SLOs, token-cost distribution, latency CDFs, and quality deltas (if reference evaluator is attached).

Safety & compliance:
- All captures must be scrubbed of customer PII at capture-time. See Security-and-Compliance checklist (link internal).
- Replays that contain production-sensitive prompts require explicit approval by the Security team; annotate manifest with "confidential=true".
- Throttle policy: default max QPS during rehearsal = 5% of observed peak for the tenant or a hard 500 RPS cap, whichever is lower.

Gameplan: Typical rehearsal run (operator checklist)
1. Select capture manifest and target environment.
2. Dry-run manifest validation (local driver, no network).
3. Provision isolated canary namespace: 2-3 nodes, same flavor as target, KVM/GPU configuration matching the change under test.
4. Start telemetry mirroring (prometheus federation job + trace sampler at 10%).
5. Run deterministic replay in three phases:
   a. Priming: replay 2 minutes of prefix/cache priming traffic at 10% speed to populate KV caches.
   b. Ramp: replay 10 minutes at 25% speed with controlled concurrency to surface queuing/backpressure.
   c. Stress validation: replay production timing for 10 minutes or until agreed inspection points.
6. Collect artifacts and run automated diff tasks.
7. If regression observed, abort and escalate; otherwise proceed to step rollouts.

Operational runbook: Step-by-step commands
- Environment prep (example):
  # create isolated namespace
  rdxctl cluster namespace create replay-canary-{{run-id}} --region us-west-2 --gpuflavor a100-80g --nodes 3

- Mirror telemetry:
  # start prom federator job (example)
  rdx-observability federate --source prometheus-prod --target prometheus-staging --labels replay_run={{run-id}}

- Start deterministic driver (YAML manifest example):
  ---
  replay_run_id: "replay-2027-01-18-42"
  source_capture: "s3://orion-captures/2027/01/09/edge-peak-1.jsonl"
  anonymize: true
  max_qps: 300
  interarrival_mode: preserved   # preserved | scaled | burst-emulate
  priming_window_seconds: 120
  phases:
    - name: priming
      scale: 0.10
      duration_seconds: 120
    - name: ramp
      scale: 0.25
      duration_seconds: 600
    - name: nominal
      scale: 1.00
      duration_seconds: 600

  # run
  rdx-replay run --manifest replay-manifest.yaml --target cluster:replay-canary-{{run-id}}

Verifications and pass/fail criteria:
- Latency: 99th percentile token response latency must not increase by > 15% vs baseline (baseline from same manifest replay against golden runtime).
- Cost: per-token compute cost must not increase by > 8% for 95% of requests.
- Error budget impact: aggregate 5xx rate must be < 0.05% during replay.
- Quality: if evaluator attached, aggregated BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity must be within configured regression tolerance (label in manifest).
- Resource utilization: GPU mem fragmentation and SM occupancy should not exceed historical peaks by > 20% without operator sign-off.

Analysis artifacts produced:
- latency-cdf.png, cost-distribution.csv, trace-diff-report.html, kv-prefix-heatmap.png, kernel-selection-log.json, batch-size-timeline.csv

Example analysis command (one-liner):
  rdx-replay analyze --run-id replay-2027-01-18-42 --baseline replay-golden-2026-11-01-08 --output /tmp/replay-analysis-42

Table: Minimum compute & storage requirements for rehearsal types
| Rehearsal type | Target parity | Min nodes | Prometheus retention | S3 capture size | Notes |
|---------------|---------------:|---------:|--------------------:|---------------:|-------|
| Quick smoke | functional | 1 | 1d | <1GB | fast checks, low fidelity |
| Canary-level | config parity | 3 | 7d | 1-10GB | matches runtime sizing for config under test |
| Full replay | production parity | N (match prod slice) | 30d | >10GB | used for incident reenactment or major infra changes |

Rollout and safety fences:
- If quick-smoke passes, schedule a canary replay with the same manifest in the target staging region.
- Automate a rollback trigger: CI/CD job creates a rollback tag and sends a Slack signal to #platform-ops if any pass/fail metric breaches.
- Gate canary-to-prod rollout on three successful WRDR runs by different engineers within 7 days.

Owner and contacts:

- Primary on-call: platform-operators rotation (see team wiki).
- Security contact: Priya Menon.

Key dashboards and alerts to enable during a run:
- replay/{{run-id}}/latency/p99 (alert if > baseline * 1.15 for 3m)
- replay/{{run-id}}/token-cost/perc95 (alert if > baseline * 1.08 for 10m)
- replay/{{run-id}}/errors/5xx-rate (alert if > 0.05%)
- replay/{{run-id}}/kernel-switch/count (informational)

Post-run retrospective template (fill-in):
1. Run-id:
2. Purpose (patch verification / incident reenactment / routine rehearsal):
3. Owners and participants:
4. Key diffs observed (latency/cost/quality):
5. Root cause hypothesis (if regression):
6. Immediate mitigations taken:
7. Follow-up actions (owners + due dates):
8. Learnings for capture design (e.g., need more long tail sequences, increase trace sampling rate):

Roadmap and open work (next 12 months):
- Integrate reference-quality evaluator to attach automated quality diffs on replay.
- Add differential tracing that stitches per-request kernel selection decisions to downstream latency.
- Support cross-region preserved-replay to validate multi-region routing policies.
- Build UI in Console for one-click replays with pre-checks and approval flow.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: replay accidentally exercises a destructive API. Mitigation: manifest validation rejects any request that targets admin endpoints and enforces a read-only overlay.
- Risk: noisy telemetry impacts production observability. Mitigation: mirror to staging observability tenants and limit federation sampling to avoid ingestion spikes.

Appendix: capture manifest best practices
- Capture window: prefer 30–90 minutes around representative peak and tail windows.
- Sampling: use deterministic sampling seeds for reproducibility.
- Anonymization rules: drop fields user.email, user_id, ip_address; hash customer_id with stable salt stored in KMS.

Appendix: quick troubleshooting
- Replay driver stalls at "priming" stage: check S3 read throughput limits, increase IAM read concurrency for replay role.
- Traces missing during run: confirm federator job is running and trace-sampler percentage > 0.
- Observability discounting: confirm labels replay_run and run_id are present so dashboards can segregate replay metrics.
